question: The most frequent mechanism that induces the activation of the BCL2 protooncogene in follicular lymphoma is:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Follicular lymphoma" -> "BCL2 protooncogene activation" -> "chromosomal translocation" -> "t(14;18) translocation" -> "BCL2 overexpression" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Follicular lymphoma" -> "BCL2 protooncogene activation" -> "gene amplification" -> "possible but rare" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Follicular lymphoma" -> "BCL2 protooncogene activation" -> "point mutation" -> "unlikely mechanism" -> 10%
analysis: The BCL2 protooncogene is most frequently activated in follicular lymphoma through a chromosomal translocation. Specifically, the t(14;18)(q32;q21) translocation is the hallmark of follicular lymphoma, which results in the juxtaposition of the BCL2 gene on chromosome 18 to the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus on chromosome 14. This translocation leads to the overexpression of the BCL2 protein, which inhibits apoptosis and contributes to the survival of the lymphoma cells.
